records.name: W. Barlow Ware
records.bio: Ware is documented in Cornell’s 2006 restoration, curation and display of the Blaschka marine invertebrate collection. Cornell’s object record credits his generosity, while his papers preserve a dedicated Blaschka project binder, photographs and collection material.

records.name: Nelson Hairston
records.bio: Hairston is named with Drew Harvell in Cornell’s 2016 project to expand and improve the Blaschka Glass Invertebrate Collection website for teaching and interdisciplinary access. His record belongs to the digital afterlife of the Cornell models.

records.name: Matthew D Shaw
records.bio: Shaw co-authored the 2017 Canterbury Museum study and illustrated catalogue of its Blaschka collection. The publication reconstructs acquisition and use while providing the project with a large object-level comparative catalogue.

records.name: Joanna Z Szczepanski
records.bio: Szczepanski co-authored the 2017 Canterbury Museum study and illustrated catalogue of its Blaschka collection. The work is a principal modern source for the collection’s acquisition, scientific context and surviving models.

records.name: Sarah F Murray
records.bio: Murray co-authored the 2017 Canterbury Museum study and illustrated catalogue of its Blaschka models. Her record marks the modern museum research through which the collection’s individual objects and historical setting were made publicly traceable.

records.name: Simon Hodge
records.bio: Hodge co-authored the 2017 Canterbury Museum study and illustrated catalogue. The publication combines collection history with an extensive model catalogue and is a key comparative source for the project’s Australasian network.

records.name: Cor J Vink
records.bio: Vink co-authored the 2017 Canterbury Museum study and illustrated catalogue of the museum’s Blaschka models. The work is an important modern inventory and collection-history anchor for Canterbury.

records.name: Rev. R. Henderson
records.bio: An incomplete Blaschka archive fragment is addressed to Henderson in Brighton and reports that the collection ordered by Frederick Wollaston Hutton for Otago Museum was nearly finished. The fragment places Henderson inside the communication chain but does not establish his exact function.
records.open: Henderson’s full identity, role, letter date and relationship to the Otago order remain unresolved.

records.name: Elizabeth Brill
records.bio: Brill is named in an official Museum of Comparative Zoology media record for the cleaning and conservation of Blaschka model MCZ:SC:152 in 2007. The record provides an object-level conservation event rather than only a general institutional treatment history.

records.name: Miss Washburn
records.roles: museum worker · mounting, cataloguing and labelling
records.bio: Boston Society of Natural History records place Miss Washburn in the practical labour of mounting, cataloguing and labelling zoological collections. The same reporting context includes Blaschka processing, making her one of the otherwise easily lost museum workers behind collection preparation.
records.open: Her full name and the object-level extent of her work on Blaschka models remain unidentified.
